newsitem.title: PERU: Peru June inflation 1.09 pct vs 0.5 pct yr-ago.
newsitem.headline: Peru June inflation 1.09 pct vs 0.5 pct yr-ago.

text.p: Peruvian consumer prices rose 1.09 percent in June, compared with a 0.5 percent rise in the same month last year and a 0.76 percent rise in May, the government's statistics agency said Tuesday.

Wholesale prices rose 0.69 percent in June, compared with a 1.0 percent rise in the same month last year and a 0.99 percent rise in May, the National Institute for Statistics and Information (INEI) announced in the official gazette, El Peruano.
Consumer prices increased 4.14 percent in the first half, compared to 6.4 percent in the January-June period last year.
Wholesale inflation for the first six months of the year was 2.55 percent, compared to 5.7 percent last year, the INEI said.

Consumer prices in Peru rose 11.8 percent in 1996, compared with a 10.2 percent rise in 1995. In 1996, cumulative inflation for wholesale prices was 11.4 percent, up from 8.80 percent the previous year.
The government estimates total consumer inflation will be nine percent this year and will drop to "the level of industrialized countries" by 2000.
